previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, status post failed kidney transplant, coronary artery disease, and chronic interstitial lung disease, was admitted with fever and substernal chest pain radiating to the chin following a dialysis session. He was febrile in the emergency department but had no focal infection signs. A CT chest showed stable chronic interstitial lung disease without pneumonia but revealed pulmonary arterial dilation suggestive of pulmonary hypertension. Blood cultures were negative, and he did not spike a fever during admission. Chest pain was consistent with chronic angina, with no troponin rise or EKG changes to suggest acute myocardial infarction. He continued his home cardiac and renal medications, completed a scheduled hemodialysis session, and remained stable. He was discharged home with instructions to follow up with his cardiologist for a planned procedure and to monitor for recurrent symptoms.
problems: Chronic total occlusion of coronary artery
Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage V or end stage renal disease

Interventional details
Mr. ___ remains reluctant to undergo CABG with SVG-RCA and 
SVG-OM. Therefore, proceeded with RCA PCI for severe ISRS. This 
vessel supplies collaterals to the chronically occluded LCX. 
Long ___ sheath and ___ AL1 guide. AC with UFH with therapeutic 
ACT. Crossed with Prowater wire with relative ease. Predilated 
with 2.5x15 mm NC balloon at 12 ATM. With difficulty, we 
delivered a 3.0x15 mm cutting balloon (had to utilize buddy-wire 
technique with ChoICE ___ XS, and deliver the balloon on the 
CPT-XS wire. Inflated the cutting balloon to 10 ATM.  Cutting 
balloon would not deflate. ST elevations noted in the inferior 
leads. Advanced the guide as close to the cutting balloon as 
possible then pulled the AL1 guide/CPT-XS wire/Prowater 
wire/cutting balloon assembly to the ascending aorta. Cutting 
balloon noted intact within the guide. The cutting 
balloon-CPT-XS assembly was then removed and inspected and found 
to be complete. Rewired with Prowater and performed additional 
POBA with 3.5x15 mm NC balloon (also utilizing buddy technique 
with CPT-XS wire. We then deployed a 3.5x18 mm Resolute 
drug-eluting stent at 12 ATM, post-dilated the distal and 
proximal overlap zones with SDS balloon at 14 and 16 ATM, 
respectively. Interim angiography showed haziness proximal to 
the new stent. Rewired the RCA and performed POBA with 3.5x15 mm 
NC balloon at 16 ATM. Angiography showed resolution of the 
hazyiness but worsening of the proximal RCA 40-50% focal lesion. 
IC NTG was administered and this focal lesion in the proximal 
RCA appeared now similar to diagnostic images, which is 
consistent with catheter-induced (guide) spasm. TIMI 3 flow was 
noted and no apparent dissection or distal embolization.The AV 
groove LCX appeared to receive rigorous collaterals from the 
RCA. The R CFA sheath was removed and ___ AngioSeal deployed with 
adequate hemostasis.  The patient left the cath lab free from 
angina and in stable
condition.

Patient will require further work up for guaiac positive stools 
as an outpatient with EGD and colonoscopy.

regularly scheduled HD on ___ and ___.  
Continued on home dose of sevelamer, Nephrocaps, and renal diet.

# Hyperkalemia- Patient had a potassium of  6.2 improved to 5.1 
on ___ after he was given calcium gluconate, insulin and 
underwent HD.  Patient again had increased K up to 6.8 likely 
due to consuming high potassium foods. This was corrected with 
dialysis. Recommended low potassium diet. 

#HTN- at home on metoprolol succinate 100mg daily and imdur 30 
mg daily, which were switched to metoprolol tartrate 50mg TID 
while in the hospital  and switched back to metoprolol succinate 
100mg daily. His imdur was increased to 60mg daily given his 
elevated blood pressures. 

CHRONIC ISSUES
# Neuropathy: continued home gabapentin.

# GERD: pantoprazole increased to 40mg BID in setting of 
possible upper GI bleed.  

TRASNITIONAL ISSUES
- ASA 81 mg indefinitely
- Clopidogrel 75 mg po daily for a minimum of 12 months. 
- Imdur increased from 30mg daily to 60mg daily for better blood 
pressure control
- pantoprazole 40mg daily increased to BID given concern of GI 
bleed
- Follow up for guaiac positive stool and may require outpatient 
endoscopy
- Encourage low potassium diet
